plan.title: Liver drug-treated vs control DE with power assessment
plan.analytical_narrative:
The input is a single bulk RNA-seq gene-level count matrix from Salmon (counts.csv, 12,000 genes x 6 samples after the gene-symbol column) with a 6-row metadata table carrying one condition column: 3 drug-treated vs 3 control human liver samples, unpaired, single batch. The research question has two halves — which genes move, and how much confidence three replicates per group buys — so the plan answers both explicitly rather than handing back a gene list alone.

T1S1 runs sample-structure QC before any model: library sizes per sample, a blind variance-stabilizing transform, PCA on the 500 most variable genes, and a sample-distance heatmap, coloured by condition. With n=3 this is the only chance to see a sample that does not sit with its group, and a single outlier here would dominate the entire result, so QC is a gate on interpretation, not decoration.

T1S2 is the primary test: minimal pre-filter (>=10 counts in >=3 samples, the smallest group size), median-of-ratios size factors estimated inside DESeq2 (counts are never pre-scaled), design ~condition with the reference level set explicitly to the control level read from metadata.csv, Wald test, apeglm shrinkage of the treated-vs-control log2 fold change, BH adjustment at alpha 0.05 with independent filtering left on. DESeq2's Cook's-distance outlier flagging sets p to NA rather than replacing counts at n=3, and those NAs must be reported separately from the ones independent filtering produces.

T1S3 addresses the confidence half of the question directly. It is a robustness and power step, not a second bite at the same test: edgeR quasi-likelihood F-test on the same counts and design, reporting each method's significant count and the intersection as the high-confidence set (never the union); a p-value histogram to check the null behaves; and a quantitative power statement grounded in the replicate-number benchmark literature — at three per group a count-based test recovers only a minority of true DE genes, concentrated at large fold changes, so absence from the list is not evidence of no change. It also runs a leave-one-out sensitivity check, refitting six times with one sample dropped, to show how much of the called set depends on any single replicate. That number is the most honest confidence statistic available for this design.

T2S1 takes the full ranked list of tested genes — every gene, not a thresholded subset — ranked by the DESeq2 Wald statistic (the disputed-metric choice is stated: the Wald stat, because it scales effect by its uncertainty and does not tie at saturated p-values), and runs fgsea against the human MSigDB hallmark collection, with GO BP as the follow-up. This matters most precisely because n=3 is underpowered: a coordinated shift across a set can be visible when no single gene clears FDR. Reactome is the canonical second collection but is not staged here; the human GO BP sets are, and the step substitutes them and says so.

T1S4 assembles the report with the fit diagnostics, both fold-change columns with the standard error, the leading-edge genes per significant set, the collection versions, and the session record. The plan does not pretend three replicates deliver a definitive gene list; it delivers a ranked, shrunken, cross-checked list with its power limit stated up front.

~ condition with explicit reference level control; contrast (condition, treated, control)
edgeR quasi-likelihood F-test as second method for robustness overlap
fgsea preranked GSEA on the DESeq2 Wald statistic against MSigDB Hallmark human, follow-up GO BP
Reproducibility and power report: MA plot, dispersion plot, p-value histogram, method overlap, power statement at n=3

GO BP follow-up run and reported, with an explicit note that Reactome was not available in this environment and GO BP was used in its place
Collection name and version (MSigDB 2026.1, human symbols) reported alongside the results
Share of ranked genes not mapping into any tested set reported
Overlapping significant sets collapsed to representatives, with the full table retained as a supplement
Random seed set and recorded, since fgsea p-values are permutation-based
constraints: Rank the full tested list; never cut it at padj or fold change before the test
Use the human collections — the mouse and rat GMTs in this environment must not be used on these human liver samples
Do not run an over-representation test on the significant gene list if fewer than about 50 genes pass padj < 0.05; report the size of that list and rely on the ranked method
Do not rank by unshrunken log2 fold change alone or by a signed p-value with ties
Set and record a random seed
caveats: Enrichment results are method-dependent; present significant sets as hypotheses for follow-up, not as established mechanism
Gene length and expression level bias set-level tests on count data; the ranked method on the tested-gene universe mitigates but does not remove this
GO BP is a nested hierarchy — parent and child sets share members, so expect correlated blocks of hits and collapse before counting findings
If a required human GMT is absent at run time, report the enrichment as not performed rather than substituting a non-human collection

grounding.reason: Preranked fgsea on the full tested list against human hallmark first (R-0107, R-0048, R-0045); disputed rank-metric R-0108 resolved to the Wald statistic per R-0099. R-0098 names Reactome as the human second collection, which is not staged in this environment — human GO BP is substituted and the substitution is reported. Counts carry HGNC symbols matching the GMT space, so the R-0101 Entrez mapping is unnecessary; the unmapped share is still reported.

steps.name: Consolidated report
steps.question: What is the defensible answer to 'which genes changed with drug treatment in these liver samples, and how confident can we be at n=3', stated with its methods, thresholds and limits?
steps.description: Assembles the final report: design and contrast, package versions, thresholds, number of genes tested and number differentially expressed, the power statement placed before the gene tables, the fit diagnostics (MA plot, dispersion plot, p-value histogram), the gene table carrying unshrunken and apeglm-shrunken log2 fold change with lfcSE and ranked by the shrunken value, the DESeq2/edgeR intersection as the high-confidence set, the leave-one-out stability numbers, the enrichment results with their collection versions and leading-edge genes, and a full reproducibility record.
steps.context: Consumes the outputs of T1S1 (QC), T1S2 (primary DE), T1S3 (robustness and power) and T2S1 (enrichment). This is where the two halves of the research question are answered together: the gene list is never presented without the power limit that qualifies it.
acceptance_criteria: Power statement at 3 replicates per group appears before the gene tables
Method, package versions, design formula, named contrast, alpha and adjustment method, number of genes tested and number DE all stated
Gene table gives log2FoldChange, apeglm-shrunken log2FoldChange and lfcSE per gene, ranked by the shrunken value, with the shrinkage estimator named in the header
MA plot, dispersion plot and p-value histogram included with a one-line reading of each
DESeq2/edgeR counts and their intersection reported; leave-one-out stability numbers included

Enrichment section names the collection, its version, the ranking metric, the universe, the size window and the tool version, and lists leading-edge genes per significant set with overlap between sets marked
Explicit statement that enrichment results are method-dependent and are hypotheses
Reproducibility record: sessionInfo, package versions, seeds, collection versions
If the significant gene list is empty or very small, the report says so plainly and does not substitute a raw-p-value list as the finding
constraints: Do not rank genes or draw plots on the unshrunken fold change alone
Do not present the union of DESeq2 and edgeR calls as the result
State the number of genes with NA padj and separate the outlier-flagged from the independent-filtering cause
Do not overstate: an underpowered negative is reported as underpowered, not as evidence of no effect
caveats: Only gene-level Salmon counts were supplied, so no transcript-length offset was applied — genes with differential isoform usage may be misestimated, and this belongs in the limitations
Single batch and 3v3 unpaired means no covariate adjustment was possible or needed; any unrecorded confounder is invisible to this design

grounding.reason: Report contents follow the returned report procedure: power statement first at n=3 (R-0094), both fold-change columns with lfcSE ranked on the shrunken value (R-0085), MA and dispersion diagnostics (R-0087), method/version/threshold reporting (R-0041, R-0051), enrichment method-dependence and leading edge (R-0055, R-0105), and the reproducibility record (R-0086).
